item.text: The executable returns Python `bytes` repr text, not raw JSON bytes, so the Node output needs to print `b'…'` exactly. I’m checking edge-case float formatting now because that is where JS and Python usually diverge.

I’ve narrowed the main compatibility issue: Python’s float text form is not the same as JS `String(number)`. The Node implementation will need a custom formatter for Python-style `repr` thresholds (`1e-05`, `1e+16`, integral values keeping `.0`, exponent padding).

item.text: Argparse has one more heuristic that matters: when `--a` expects a value, a following token that starts with `-` is only treated as a value if it looks like a negative number. That means `--a -3.14` works, but `--a -h`, `--a -foo`, and even `--a -1_2` all fail with “expected one argument”.
